questions.prompt: What is the periodic table?
questions.explanation: The periodic table is a system for arranging all the chemical elements in order of atomic number.

options: A system for arranging all the chemical elements
A list of only the metals

questions.prompt: What is the atomic number of an element?
questions.explanation: The atomic number is the number of protons in an atom.

options: The number of protons plus electrons
The number of protons in an atom

questions.prompt: What is a period in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: A period is a horizontal row; elements are placed left to right by increasing atomic number.

questions.prompt: What is a group in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: A group is a vertical column; its elements share the same number of outer-shell electrons.

questions.prompt: How does the atomic number change across a period from left to right?
questions.explanation: Across a period the atomic number increases by one from each element to the next.

questions.prompt: Which two elements make up the very short first period?
questions.explanation: The first period is very short and contains only hydrogen and helium.

questions.prompt: How many elements are in the sixth period?
questions.explanation: The sixth period contains 32 elements.

questions.prompt: Why do all elements in a group behave similarly in reactions?
questions.explanation: Chemical behaviour depends on outer electrons, and a group shares the same number of them.

options: They have the same number of outer-shell electrons
They have the same number of shells

questions.prompt: What is the name of Group I?
questions.explanation: Group I is the alkali metals; each has one outer electron and is very reactive.

questions.prompt: How does reactivity change down Group I?
questions.explanation: In Group I reactivity increases down the group — the bottom elements are the most reactive.

questions.prompt: How does potassium react with water?
questions.explanation: Potassium is a soft, very reactive alkali metal that reacts violently with water.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Group II?
questions.explanation: Group II is the alkaline earth metals; each has two outer electrons.

questions.prompt: How does magnesium react with cold water compared with steam?
questions.explanation: Magnesium reacts quite slowly with cold water but more quickly with steam.

options: Slowly with cold water, faster with steam

questions.prompt: What is the name of Group VII?
questions.explanation: Group VII is the halogens — very reactive, coloured, poisonous elements.

questions.prompt: Why are halogens very reactive?
questions.explanation: Halogens have 7 outer electrons — one empty space — so they easily gain an electron.

options: Their atoms have one empty space in the outer shell

questions.prompt: How does reactivity change down the halogens (Group VII)?
questions.explanation: In the halogens the top elements are most reactive, so reactivity decreases down the group.

questions.prompt: What is bromine?
questions.explanation: Bromine is a harmful red liquid (a halogen) that turns into a brown gas.

options: A red liquid that turns into a brown gas

questions.prompt: What do CFCs (a halogen compound) damage?
questions.explanation: CFCs break down the ozone layer, which protects us from harmful ultraviolet radiation.

questions.prompt: What useful property of chlorine is used in drinking water?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is added to drinking water in small quantities because it disinfects it.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Group VIII (Group 0)?
questions.explanation: Group VIII/0 is the noble gases — unreactive because their outer shells are full.

questions.prompt: Why do noble gases not react?
questions.explanation: Noble gases have completely full outer shells, which makes them stable and unreactive.

options: Their outer electron shells are full

questions.prompt: Why is helium used in balloons?
questions.explanation: Helium is safe (unreactive) and much lighter than air, so it is used for balloons.

options: It is unreactive and lighter than air

questions.prompt: What separates the metals from the non-metals on the periodic table?
questions.explanation: A stepped line divides the metals (left) from the non-metals (right).

questions.prompt: Why is silicon called a metalloid (semi-metal)?
questions.explanation: Silicon is a metalloid because it shares some properties with metals and some with non-metals.

options: It has some metal and some non-metal properties

questions.prompt: Which word means "can be hammered into shape"?
questions.explanation: Malleable means a material can be hammered or bent into shape without breaking.

questions.prompt: Which word means "can be pulled into wires"?
questions.explanation: Ductile means a material can be drawn (pulled) into wires — e.g. tungsten and copper.

questions.prompt: Which word means "makes a ringing sound when hit"?
questions.explanation: Sonorous means a material rings when struck — e.g. brass, used for bells.

questions.prompt: Why is lead used to waterproof roofs?
questions.explanation: Lead is malleable, so it can be bent and shaped to waterproof a roof.

options: It is malleable, so it can be shaped

questions.prompt: Why is tungsten used for light-bulb filaments?
questions.explanation: Tungsten has high resistance so it glows when current passes, and it is ductile enough to form thin wire.

options: It has high resistance and glows, and is ductile

questions.prompt: Why is copper used for electrical wires?
questions.explanation: Copper is a very good conductor of electricity and is ductile, so it is used for wires.

options: It is a very good conductor of electricity

questions.prompt: Why is aluminium used for saucepans?
questions.explanation: Aluminium conducts heat well, which makes it ideal for saucepans and cooking utensils.

options: It is a good conductor of sound
It is a good conductor of heat

questions.prompt: What is brass made from?
questions.explanation: Brass is a sonorous alloy of copper and zinc, used for instruments and bells.

questions.prompt: What is steel an alloy of?
questions.explanation: Steel is an alloy of iron; it is strong and withstands high temperatures.

questions.prompt: Why is iron used to build bridges?
questions.explanation: Iron is used for bridges because it is strong.
